properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Unit-test-side MD5 for HTTP Digest authentication: tests/unit_tests/http.cpp implements md5_hex() (EVP_DigestInit with EVP_md5, lines 312-325) and computes the RFC 2617 A1/A2/response digests (lines 1483-1484 etc.) to exercise epee's HTTP Digest auth. MD5 is the digest-auth legacy algorithm; the production instantiation of the same algorithm is http_auth.cpp:166 (struct md5_ : digest_base_<EVP_md5, 16>), reported separately since the collectors only saw the test file.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Polyseed wallet-seed KDF: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (implemented over libsodium's crypto_auth_hmacsha256) derives the wallet key from the normalized seed phrase. The iteration count is fixed by the upstream polyseed library (external build dependency, polyseed spec) and passed in as parameter c — not visible in this tree. PBKDF2-SHA256 is the memoryless legacy KDF (Argon2-class memory-hardness would be stronger), but the algorithm is fixed by the polyseed seed format for cross-wallet compatibility — ob

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: epee TLS peer-verification posture for daemon/wallet P2P+RPC: client-side cert verification can be turned off with --ssl-allow-any-cert (ssl_verification_t::none), and by default the server side never inspects client certificates unless operator-configured fingerprints or a CA path are present. Changeable here (runtime flag / ssl_options_t defaults).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same PBKDF2 implementation (pbkdf2.c/h): iteration count c is a caller-supplied parameter — the upstream polyseed library chooses it per its spec, so the 'low iterations' figure is not determinable from this repository. The KDF itself is real and live (wired at polyseed.cpp:84).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 ECDSA / curve arithmetic as pulled in by the k256 0.13.4 dependency of the fcmp_pp prototype (same lockfile entry as LIB-1f90954c). Shor-vulnerable signature family used in the proof prototype.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: gen_ssl_cert utility encrypts the generated TLS private key at rest with AES-128-CFB (PEM/PKCS8, EVP_aes_128_cfb) when an operator supplies a passphrase — unauthenticated stream cipher mode, 128-bit key. Changeable here (could move to aes-256-cfb or a PEM format supporting AEAD). Classical risk profile; not quantum-relevant (symmetric).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: python-rpc functional-test framework credential: a placeholder wallet password ('custom-background-password') hardcoded in the test framework used to drive test wallets. Dev/test tooling only — never a production secret; hardcoded by design for reproducible test runs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The ECDH-family key-agreement surface of Monero, in three groups: (1) TLS 1.2 ECDHE cipher suites (net_ssl.cpp:215) — ephemeral elliptic-curve key exchange for all daemon/wallet P2P+RPC traffic; harvest-now-decrypt-later surface, migration hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768; (2) ringct ecdhEncode/ecdhDecode — transaction amount/mask masking (device.hpp:220-221 interface, device_default.cpp:390-391 software impl, device_ledger.cpp:1860-1866 Ledger impl, trezor protocol.cpp:666-700 signing flow), keyed by p

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The ref10-derived Ed25519 builder (src/crypto/crypto_ops_builder) — the source scaffolding from which Monero's shipped crypto-ops.c is generated: fe25519/ge25519/sc25519 arithmetic, ed25519 core, and randombytes.c (reads /dev/urandom as the builder's CSPRNG). This is the implementation root of Monero's Shor-vulnerable signature/key-image/key-derivation machinery (EdDSA-style ops on the edwards25519-variant curve); migration path ML-DSA/SLH-DSA for signatures and ML-KEM for the derivation-style a

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Monero's own edwards25519→Curve25519 (Montgomery) conversion helpers in the ref10-derived crypto-ops library (src/crypto/crypto-ops.c:3921-3951, declarations crypto-ops.h:181): edwardsYZ_to_x25519, ge_p3_to_x25519, edwards_bytes_to_x25519_vartime. These convert CryptoNote output keys to X25519 form — curve arithmetic on a Shor-vulnerable curve; migration path ML-KEM-768 for any agreement built on it. Changeable here (part of the shipped protocol library).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDHE-ECDSA suites in the epee TLS 1.2 cipher list (net_ssl.cpp:215): ECDSA certificate authentication is offered on all daemon/wallet TLS (usable when the operator supplies an ECDSA cert; the auto-generated self-signed cert is RSA). ECDSA is Shor-vulnerable — signature migration path ML-DSA/SLH-DSA, distinct from the ECDHE key-exchange migration.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Curve25519 arithmetic as pulled in by the curve25519-dalek 4.1.3 dependency of the fcmp_pp prototype (same lockfile entry as LIB-f69df116). Shor-vulnerable curve ops used for the prototype's tree/proof arithmetic.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: This is the enforced minimum TLS protocol version for every epee TLS endpoint (daemon P2P, daemon RPC, wallet RPC): net_ssl.cpp:211-212 set no_tlsv1/no_tlsv1_1 on the sslv23 context ("only allow tls v1.2 and up", comment at :207). This net.cpp test parameter exercises that floor. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Monero's primary hash function: Keccak-1600 with the pre-standardization Keccak padding (predecessor of SHA-3, not identical to the final SHA-3 standard). This is the dominant hash asset of the codebase: cn_fast_hash / cn_fast_hash_128 (hash.c:40-50, keccakf/keccak1600), the vendored permutation (keccak.c), HMAC-Keccak (hmac-keccak.c:35+), and ~200 sites across the protocol — block/transaction IDs, ring-signature challenge derivation (hash_to_scalar), key-derivation-to-scalar, ringct, wallet cac

The ~140 sites are implementation internals plu

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 in four roles across the codebase: (1) self-signed X.509 signing digest — X509_sign(cert, pkey, EVP_sha256()) at net_ssl.cpp:179 (pairs with the RSA-4096 keygen); (2) certificate fingerprinting for TLS pinning — X509_digest(EVP_sha256()) net_ssl.cpp:371 and get_hr_ssl_fingerprint_from_file net_ssl.h:186; (3) generic SHA-256 helpers in src/common/util.cpp:689/703 (EVP_Digest); (4) the HMAC core of polyseed's PBKDF2 (pbkdf2.c:56). All strong-symmetric, quantum-safe; recorded for coverage.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The HMAC-SHA256 layer under polyseed's PBKDF2: libsodium crypto_auth_hmacsha256_init/update/final calls implement the inner/outer HMAC in the PBKDF2 loop (pbkdf2.c:47-89). Quantum-safe MAC; also the primitive backing the wallet-seed KDF.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Polyseed wallet-seed KDF wiring: polyseed.cpp:84 installs crypto_pbkdf2_sha256 (implementation pbkdf2.c over libsodium HMAC-SHA256) as the polyseed library's PBKDF2, which derives the wallet key from the normalized seed phrase + birthdate salt. Iteration count is fixed by the upstream polyseed library spec (external build dependency, polyseed_static), not visible in-tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256/SHA-512 as pulled in by the sha2 0.10.9 dependency of the fcmp_pp prototype (same lockfile entry as LIB-ea6b9ac4). Quantum-safe hashing used by the prototype's transcript/tree hashing.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-256 in two distinct roles: (1) ECDHE-ECDSA/RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 suites in the epee TLS 1.2 cipher list (net_ssl.cpp:215) — strong AEAD, quantum-safe symmetric half; (2) AES-256 round helpers (aes_256_assist1/2 and callers, slow-hash.c:541-601) inside the AES-NI variant of Monero's CryptoNight PoW slow-hash — bulk primitive used for proof-of-work, not confidentiality. Both are live code the build ships.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Secure randomness source for HTTP Digest authentication: RAND_bytes (OpenSSL CSPRNG) generates the server nonce and client cnonce material in epee's HTTP auth. Not a weakness — an inventory-worthy DRBG asset showing where auth randomness comes from. Quantum-safe.

Shor-vulnerable curve; changeable here (prototype dependency, not consensus-bound).
